title: API and stream replica failover
description: An api replica killed mid-film loses neither the picture nor the resume position; WebSockets reconnect to any replica. The stream role carries every byte and is in no failure test: kill and roll a stream replica too, for HLS and direct play. On SIGTERM a replica fails readiness first, then drains for a grace that matches the pod's termination grace period.
acceptanceCriteria: e2e, api kill: with two api replicas behind the router, SIGKILL the one holding the viewer's socket (sessions.ws_replica names it) while a film plays: the film plays at least 30 s past the kill on the same player, with no Playback Error dialog, no sign-in page and no new PlaybackInfo

Progress persists through that kill: every Progress and Stopped report the browser sends after it is answered 2xx by the live replica (only a request in flight on the killed replica may fail), and once the viewer stops, the film's resume position is where they stopped, past the position at the kill, and playing it again resumes there

The socket reconnects: after that kill the browser has an open /socket again on a live replica (the survivor, or one started since), which sent it ForceKeepAlive, while the film still plays and without the viewer reloading or signing in

Ownership moves: once a device's socket is open on a live replica, sessions.ws_replica names that replica and never the killed one again, also after the new socket closes (then NULL, or the device's newest socket on another live replica)

A device that does not reconnect: within two minutes of the kill sessions.ws_replica names no killed replica, with no socket of the device having to close first; a device with sockets on two replicas whose newer one was on the killed replica is then owned by the live one
A replica stopped with SIGTERM closes its WebSockets and removes their session_sockets rows before it exits: clients see the close, and from its exit sessions.ws_replica names it for no device

e2e, stream kill, HLS: with two stream replicas behind the router, SIGKILL one that is serving a transcoding film's segments: the film plays past everything the player had buffered at the kill, on segments the other replica serves, on the same player, with no Playback Error dialog and no new PlaybackInfo

e2e, stream kill, direct play: SIGKILL the stream replica that is sending a film still being downloaded: the film plays past everything buffered at the kill, on ranges the other replica serves, with no Playback Error dialog, and stays a direct play (no new PlaybackInfo, no transcode)

e2e, stream roll, HLS and direct play: the same two kinds of film each play past everything buffered when one stream replica gets SIGTERM and a replacement is started; in the HLS case no playlist or segment request fails or is answered 400 or more, and the replacement serves the film once it is ready

Readiness is its own route, answered without a token by api and stream replicas alike: 200 while the replica takes requests; GET /healthz goes on answering 2xx through a drain and through a Postgres outage of any length

On SIGTERM readiness answers 503 from then on, before anything is refused: for a documented time after the first 503 the replica still accepts new requests and answers them normally, so a router that polls readiness loses none

Responses in flight when it stops accepting (a segment waiting on its job, a direct-play range mid-body) are sent whole if they end within the grace, and the process then exits by itself; one that outlasts the grace is cut at its end and the process exits within seconds of it, so a slow or hung client never holds a replica

The grace is one config setting with a documented default: the exit time of a replica with an endless response follows two different values, a value that is not a duration or is negative is refused at start, and docs/running.md says to set the pod's termination grace period above it

Postgres away for less than a switchover: readiness stays 200 (still 200 at 20 s away), requests wait and are answered without an error once it is back, as before; several short outages that add up to more than 30 s never fail readiness

Postgres away continuously for longer (503 by 40 s): readiness fails only on the replicas that cannot reach it, requests already waiting go on waiting as before (a segment up to 90 s), and readiness is 200 again within seconds of Postgres answering, with no restart

SIGTERM while Postgres is away, before or after readiness has failed for it: readiness is 503 at once and the process exits by the end of the grace, though its requests wait on the database and its socket rows cannot be removed
